instruction: Implement `export function parseCsvLine(line: string): string[]` in this file, replacing the stub. Parse ONE CSV line into fields: comma-separated; a double-quoted field may contain literal commas; a doubled quote "" inside quotes is a literal quote; empty and trailing-empty fields preserved. Examples: parseCsvLine("a,b,c")=["a","b","c"]; parseCsvLine('a,"b,c",d')=["a","b,c","d"]; parseCsvLine('"a""b"')=['a"b']. Edit only this file.

_verification: TS twin of t25-csv-parse (Rust). Same spec, different language — to test whether local models do better on TS than Rust. Oracle RED->GREEN confirmed 2026-06-08; gates on node --test behavioral exit (tsc type-noise ignored).

observed_baseline._finding: TS twin of t25-csv-parse (Rust). The two models that FAILED the Rust CSV (qwen 0/5, gpt-oss 0/5) recover in TypeScript — the Rust borrow-checker/idioms were a real factor, not just the parsing logic. devstral strong in both. Language matters: a Rust-only benchmark overstates the local-model ceiling.
observed_baseline._comparison: vs Rust t25-csv-parse (react): qwen 0/5→2/3 · gpt-oss 0/5→1/3 · devstral 5/5→3/3 · gemma3 4/5→2/3. The Rust-FAILURES (qwen, gpt-oss) recover in TS; models already-capable in Rust stay comparable.
